title: House of Assassins
author: Larry Correia
review: So fun, badass, and metal. Exceeded expectations.

highlights.text: “Even when you aren’t feeling strong, you must never ever show weakness. Victims want pity. Warriors demand respect.
“What sad manner of prophet doesn’t believe in their own prophecies?”
“Even if Angruvadal had not shattered, it wouldn’t have found you worthy. You should never have come here.”
Freedom was a myth. There was Law and consequences. That was all.
Your next few words will determine whether you die quick and painless, or with a buzzard’s beak scissoring through your guts, so I would encourage you to answer truthfully.”
It was difficult, getting to know those you were supposed to hate.
I would advise choosing the wiser path.” “What do you mean by wiser path?” “Take the one that does not place you as my adversary…”
“If your fight is fair, then your tactics were stupid.”
He was known for being good at two things. Solving crimes, and then bashing the criminals responsible with his war hammer. He preferred the latter to the former.
“These are perilous times.” “Truth. We were just planning on how best to hunt down and kill someone I respect more than anyone else in the world.”
“To an old friend.” Devedas raised his glass. “May we kill him speedily.”
“You know why men of honor are so rare these days? They all die pointlessly for no good reason.
Determination rarely beats skill, and determination alone never beats skill and determination…”
“This is only a bad dream,” Ashok whispered. “Go back to sleep. You would not want to meet me in the waking world.”
In the warrior caste there was no shortage of old cowards with chests full of medals, and graveyards filled with young heroes.
So there were probably no such thing as gods, but fate…A warrior knew that fate was real…She was a stone-hearted bitch.

“I just murdered Protector of the Law Ishaan Harban, who I loved like a brother. Yet I stabbed him in the heart because he got in my way. I care nothing about any of you. Now open this gate or I will tear it down!”
never underestimate anyone who got old in a job where most die young.
Since they had found a way to proceed without the wizard’s help, it made Ashok glad that he’d killed him. Improper equipment maintenance was an indication of poor character.
The gods don’t care if you’re a good man any more than the Law did. They just need a killer, and killing is all you’ll ever be good for…And that just kind of makes me sad.”
There’s crime because it’s against the Law. And then there’s crime because it’s just plain wrong.
Keta’s gods seemed to will a great many things, but it was men with sweat on their brow and calluses on their hands that did the work.
The world shook. Bone piles toppled. Crazed images flashed through Thera’s mind as ancient gods collided inside her head.

“I do not challenge…But I fear for the future of our house.” “Of course you do,” Sikasso snapped. “You’ve lived your entire life in fear. You hide it well, Kabir, but your doubts plague you and render you weak.”
When gods collide, the last place you wanted to be was caught between them.

The gods had grown old and weak, a tiny fragment of what they’d once been, but all their hatred remained. If they couldn’t destroy each other, they’d use their children to destroy in their name. These weren’t even the real gods, they were partial gods, shadows of shadows, distorted echoes of a sound that had happened a long time ago.

She saw the War in Heaven, forces beyond her comprehension clashing. That was when this piece of the darkness had been torn from the rest of itself, and hurled down in a ball of fire, amid a rain of demons. It had struck the ground so hard that it had dug a crater which had filled with water. Broken, it had died. Its children had sensed its presence and come to worship. Some of them chose to die here next to the piece of their fallen god, because its darkness reminded them of home.
Ashok did not fear death. He’d done it once already today,
“There is only one man in Lok who does not know fear. Of course you’re afraid. Fear is the tool that keeps most alive. Now you must be afraid for her as well.”
“Heed me, demons. I am Ashok Vadal. You are guilty of trespass. Return to the sea now and I will spare your lives. Stay and I will kill you all.”

The smiling fat man seemed pleased. Ashok did not think the smiling fat man was the Forgotten. The Forgotten did not strike him as a kind god. Anyone who would choose Ashok Vadal to be his warrior would never be portrayed as kind.
The strong will replace those we’ve lost, and the weak will be our slaves. We will survive this. It’s what we do.” Ashok coughed up blood. “Evil.” “Perhaps.”
